                    ### Question
                    A 26-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of a 3-day history of nausea and vomiting. Her last menstrual period was 9 weeks ago. A urine pregnancy test is positive. Ultrasonography shows an intrauterine pregnancy consistent in size with a 7-week gestation. The hormone that was measured in this patient's urine to detect the pregnancy is also directly responsible for which of the following processes?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Maintenance of the corpus luteum
opb. Inhibition of ovulation
opc. Development of breast tissue
opd. Inhibition of preterm uterine contractions
ope. Preparation of the uterine endometrium for implantation

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) is responsible for the maintenance of the corpus luteum, not the preparation of the uterine endometrium for implantation. This hormone supports the corpus luteum to continue producing progesterone, which is crucial for early pregnancy support.
